Evidence, access reviews, vulnerabilities, secret rotations and certificates.

| At a glance          |                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Endpoint**         | `https://g8deck.app/mcp/compliance`                                                                                      |
| **Server name**      | `g8deck-compliance`                                                                                                      |
| **Who can reach it** | Ops only. Reaching it needs `mcp.access.compliance`, which no customer role holds.                                       |
| **Authentication**   | A personal access token (`Authorization: Bearer …`) or OAuth 2.1 sign-in — see [Connect an AI client](/docs/mcp/connect) |
| **Route limit**      | 30 requests per minute                                                                                                   |
| **Tools**            | 12 — 8 read, 3 write, 1 destroy                                                                                          |

Every tool needs a token carrying its tier: `mcp:read`, `mcp:write` or `mcp:destroy`, each tier including the ones before it. On top of the route limit, each caller gets 60 read, 20 write and 5 destroy calls a minute. Your role decides which tools answer at all; a tool you can see but lack the permission for answers `permission_denied` and names the permission. Secret and credential values never cross this boundary — tools take them inbound and report key names only.

## What the client is told

The server sends these instructions to every AI client that connects, before any tool is called. They are reproduced verbatim because they carry the reading rules that change what an answer means.

<details class="instructions">
<summary>Server instructions</summary>

```text
G8Deck compliance server — evidence, access reviews, vulnerabilities and certificates. Ops-only.

Conventions:
- Reaching this server needs `mcp.access.compliance`, which no customer role holds.
- Everything is identified by uuid. Every tool accepts an optional `organization` and echoes the one it used.
- **Secret values never cross this boundary.** `list-secret-rotations` reports which secret, which versions and how long the old value is still accepted — never the value.

Reading rules that change what an answer means:
- **Unscanned is not clean.** An image that could not be scanned records nothing. An empty vulnerability list may mean nothing was found or nothing was looked at — check whether a scan ran.
- **An unknown CVE severity stays unknown.** It is never mapped down to low: recording "we could not establish severity" as the least serious level launders an unknown into a reassurance.
- **`no_recorded_activity` is not "inactive".** There is no last-login column; the audit trail records actions, so someone who signs in and only reads leaves no trace. Absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.
- **A control with no evidence is unevidenced, not failing.** The two need different responses.
- **An overdue breach clock reports negative hours.** It is not clamped to zero, because overdue is the most important thing it can say.
- **Data residency treats an unrecorded provider location as a violation** — an unknown region cannot be shown to be compliant. An organisation with no policy at all is unconstrained, which is a different state.

Writes:
- `acknowledge-vulnerability` is scoped to ONE deployment. Accepting a risk on staging does not silence the same CVE in production.
- `open-access-review` is idempotent: an already-open session is returned rather than a second created.
- `revoke-certificate` is destructive, needs the domain retyped and a token carrying `mcp:destroy`, and leaves the domain without TLS.
```

</details>

## Read tools

### `whoami`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code></p>

Report who you are: identity, roles, which MCP servers you may reach, your token's abilities, the organisations you can address and which one is used when you omit the `organization` argument. Call this first.

Takes no parameters.

### `get-audit-trail`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>security.view.audit-logs</code></p>

The audit trail, filterable by event, actor, auditable type and date range. These rows are immutable by construction — no soft deletes, no hard deletes.

| Parameter        | Type    | Description                                                            |
| ---------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `event`          | string  | Exact event name, e.g. created, quota_denied, mcp_cross_tenant_access. |
| `auditable_type` | string  | Partial model class name, e.g. Deployment.                             |
| `actor_email`    | string  | Partial actor email.                                                   |
| `from`           | string  | Only records on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).                       |
| `to`             | string  | Only records on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).                      |
| `organization`   | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.      |
| `page`           | integer | Page number, starting at 1.                                            |
| `per_page`       | integer | Results per page, 1-100 (default 50).                                  |

### `list-access-reviews`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>security.manage.access-control</code></p>

Access review sessions for this organisation (SOC 2 CC6.2), newest first.

| Parameter      | Type   | Description                                                       |
| -------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `organization` | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `get-access-review`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>security.manage.access-control</code></p>

One access review with its member snapshot and decisions. Members with no recorded activity are flagged `no_recorded_activity` — NOT "inactive": there is no last-login column, only an audit trail of actions, so someone who signs in and reads leaves no trace.

| Parameter                                  | Type   | Description                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `review` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Access review session uuid.                                       |
| `organization`                             | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `list-vulnerabilities`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>security.view.audit-logs</code></p>

CVEs recorded against this organisation's deployments. Two things this deliberately does NOT do: it never maps an unknown severity down to low, and an image that could not be scanned records nothing rather than a clean result — unscanned and scanned-and-clean must never look the same.

| Parameter      | Type    | Description                                                         |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `severity`     | string  | Filter by severity. One of: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical`.    |
| `status`       | string  | Filter by status. One of: `open`, `patched`, `accepted`, `ignored`. |
| `deployment`   | string  | Deployment uuid or slug.                                            |
| `organization` | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.   |
| `page`         | integer | Page number, starting at 1.                                         |
| `per_page`     | integer | Results per page, 1-100 (default 20).                               |

### `list-certificates`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>deployments.view.certificates</code></p>

SSL certificates across this organisation's deployments: domain, source, expiry and auto-renew. Private key and certificate material never cross this boundary.

| Parameter              | Type    | Description                                                       |
| ---------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `expiring_within_days` | integer | Only certificates expiring within this many days.                 |
| `deployment`           | string  | Deployment uuid or slug.                                          |
| `organization`         | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `list-secret-rotations`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>security.manage.access-control</code></p>

Secret rotations and their overlap windows. Values are NEVER returned — only which secret, which versions, and until when the old value is still accepted. A rotation without an overlap window is an outage somebody scheduled.

| Parameter      | Type    | Description                                                       |
| -------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open_only`    | boolean | Only rotations whose overlap window is still open.                |
| `organization` | string  | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `get-compliance-status`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:read</code> · permission <code>security.view.audit-logs</code></p>

SOC 2 control coverage and PDPA position for this organisation, with the evidence recorded against each control. An overdue breach clock reports NEGATIVE hours rather than clamping to zero — overdue is the most important thing it can say.

| Parameter      | Type   | Description                                                       |
| -------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `organization` | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

## Write tools

### `open-access-review`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>security.manage.access-control</code></p>

Open an access review for this organisation, snapshotting the current membership. Idempotent: if one is already open it is returned rather than a second being created — two open sessions mean two reviewers working from different lists, and the last to finish silently overwrites the other.

| Parameter      | Type   | Description                                                       |
| -------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `organization` | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `acknowledge-vulnerability`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>security.manage.access-control</code></p>

Accept the risk of one CVE on ONE deployment, with a reason. Acknowledging on staging does not silence the same CVE in production — the two are separate records and separate decisions.

| Parameter                                      | Type   | Description                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deployment` <span class="req">required</span> | string | Deployment uuid or slug the risk is accepted on.                  |
| `cve_id` <span class="req">required</span>     | string | CVE identifier, e.g. CVE-2025-1234.                               |
| `reason` <span class="req">required</span>     | string | Why the risk is accepted. Recorded with the acknowledgement.      |
| `organization`                                 | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

### `export-compliance-evidence`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:write</code> · permission <code>security.view.audit-logs</code></p>

Export the evidence recorded against one SOC 2 control for a period. Returns the evidence set, and names the sources it SEARCHED — a response with three sections is otherwise indistinguishable from one where the other lookups silently failed.

| Parameter                                      | Type   | Description                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `control_id` <span class="req">required</span> | string | SOC 2 control id, e.g. CC6.2 (see get-compliance-status).         |
| `period` <span class="req">required</span>     | string | Period label, e.g. 2026-Q3 or 2026-08.                            |
| `organization`                                 | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation. |

## Destructive tools

Each needs a token carrying `mcp:destroy`, and most also need an identifying value retyped into a confirmation argument. A mismatch is refused and audited.

### `revoke-certificate`

<p class="tool-meta">Tier <code>mcp:destroy</code> · permission <code>deployments.manage.certificates</code></p>

Revoke a certificate and stop it renewing. The domain stops serving TLS until a replacement is issued — and Let's Encrypt rate-limits five failed validations per hostname per hour, so a re-issue is not guaranteed to be immediate. Requires the domain retyped in confirm_name.

| Parameter                                        | Type   | Description                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `certificate` <span class="req">required</span>  | string | Certificate uuid.                                                              |
| `confirm_name` <span class="req">required</span> | string | The certificate's exact domain, retyped. Anything else is refused and audited. |
| `organization`                                   | string | Organisation uuid or slug. Omit to use your default organisation.              |
